The '''Atrek''' ({{langx|fa|اترک}}, {{langx|ku-Latn|Etrek}}, {{langx|tk|Etrek}}), also known as the '''Attrack''',<ref>"[[:s:Encyclopædia Britannica, Ninth Edition/Atrek|Atrek]]" in the ''Encyclopædia Britannica'', {{nowrap|9th ed.}} 1878.</ref> '''Atrak''', and '''Etrek''', is a fast-moving river which begins in the mountains of north-eastern [[Iran]] ({{coord|37|10|N|59|00|E|}}) and flows {{convert|563|km|mi}} westward, draining into the south-eastern corner of the [[Caspian Sea]] in [[Turkmenistan]]. Because of the high use of its waters for irrigation, the Atrek only flows into the Caspian when it is in its flood stage."}}
